Data stores have types they inherit from the zone to which they belong. Later, data stores can be attached to a hypervisor (compute resource)/compute zone of the same type. Data stores can be moved from one data store zone to another, but the zones should have the same type. For more information, refer to Zone types. Use caution when changing data store settings. To use the data store, add it to a data store zone and assign it either to a hypervisor (compute resource) or a compute zone. A QCOW2 data store can be assigned only to the Virtuozzo Server 9 hypervisor (compute resource) where it is located. To create a QCOW2 data store Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Data Stores icon. Click the Create Data Store button in the lower-right corner and fill in the following: Step 1 of 2. Properties Label - enter the data store label. Data store type - select qcow2. Enabled - move the slider to the right to turn on the data store. If disabled, new disks are forbidden to be created automatically on the data store.

chunks.title: Managing hypervisor (compute resource) data store
chunks.content: Managing hypervisor (compute resource) data store Data stores can easily be attached and removed from hypervisors (compute resources). This association between a hypervisor (compute resource) and a data store is called a data store join. Hypervisors (compute resources) running Virtuozzo Server 9 support LVM and QCOW2 data store types. To remove a data store join Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Compute Resources icon. Click the label of the hypervisor (compute resource) you want to manage data stores for. On the following page, click the Actions button, point to Management Options, and select Manage Data Stores. Click the Detach Data Store button () next to the desired data store join. In the dialog, click OK. To add a data store join Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Compute Resources icon. Click the label of the hypervisor (compute resource) you want to manage data stores for. On the following page, click the Actions button, point to Management Options, and select Manage Data Stores. In the Add Data Store section, fill in the following:Data store - in the drop-down list, choose the desired one. Click the Add Data Store button in the lower-right corner. You can add data stores to a hypervisor (compute resource) only if assigned to zones of the same type. For more information, refer to Zone types.

chunks.title: Data store zone settings
chunks.content: Data store zone settings Data store zones can be used to create different service tiers–for example, by setting up different zones for ordinary and high-performance SANs. Data store zones have types inherited by the data stores in the zone. Later, data stores can be attached to a hypervisor (compute resource)/compute zone of the same type. Data stores can be moved from one data store zone to another, but the zones should have the same type. For more information, refer to Zone types. The table below demonstrates the available data store zone types for different data stores: Data store type Data store zone type QCOW2 Virtual LVM Virtual A data store zone consists of several data stores sharing the same permissions. Data store zones can be used to create different tiers of service. Zones can also be used to create private clouds for specific users. This section contains information on how to create data stores and manage them within their data store zone. To create a data store zone Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Data Store Zones icon. Click the Create Data Store Zone button () or the Create Data Store Zone button in the lower-right corner. On the screen that follows:Label - give your data store zone a name. Server type - choose the server type from the drop-down list:Choose the virtual server type to create a KVM zone. The zone’s type cannot be changed after the zone is created. Click Save.

chunks.title: Managing virtual machine disks
chunks.content: Managing virtual machine disks Virtual machine storage is provided by disks. A disk is a partition of a data store that is allocated to a specific virtual machine. Disks can be assigned as the standard or swap disks (there are no swap disks for Windows-based templates). They can also be set as primary (that is, the disk from which an OS will boot). Managing disks for the entire cloud is handled through the Control Panel’s Settings menu. Disks for individual virtual machines are managed through the Control Panel > Cloud > Virtual Servers menu, where you can: Add disks to a virtual machine Edit virtual machine disks Migrate virtual machine disks Assign a disk to a VM Delete virtual machine disks Do not create multiple partitions on one disk for virtual machines. Control Panel supports only one partition per disk. In cases when you change disk partition, the CP might lose control of such a disk and the VM associated with it. If required, create additional disks instead. Add disks to virtual machines Adding a disk to a virtual machine will require that VM should be rebooted. If a VM is running when you try to add a new disk to it, you’ll be asked to confirm the reboot. To add a disk to a virtual machine Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Virtual Servers menu. Click a VM’s label to open its details screen. Go to the Storage > Disks tab. Click the Add button () or the Create Disk button in the lower-right corner. Fill in the details:Specify disk label.

chunks.title: Cloud search tool
chunks.content: Cloud search tool The search tool in the upper left corner allows you to search your cloud for: IP addresses Usernames Users full names (first or last name, in any order) VM labels VM identifiers Disk identifiers Log IDs Backups Template labels Permission labels/identifiers Page URLs/titles Any word from locale texts (yellow help box texts), if other search results are not successful Type what you want to search for into the search box and confirm. The results are organized according to the menu item they refer to—for example, Pages, Virtual Servers, Users, Locales, etc. Click a search result to open the relevant details page.

chunks.title: Help
chunks.content: Help The Help menu enables you and your users to submit support requests to the Virtuozzo team. All Virtuozzo customers with a full license are entitled to 24/7 support. To submit a support request, go to your Control Panel > Admin > Help menu and complete the form. Alternatively, you can use the Virtuozzo Support Portal. Be aware that the Help menu enables your users to submit requests to Virtuozzo on behalf of the cloud owner. All the requests received via Help are considered to be sent from a trusted source. You can prohibit certain users or user groups from accessing the Help menu using the corresponding permissions.

chunks.title: Managing hypervisors (compute resources)
chunks.content: Managing hypervisors (compute resources) Hypervisors (compute resources) are based on KVM virtualization and run with Virtuozzo Server 9 or CentOS 7 as a management operating system. Hypervisors (compute resources) are used to provide hardware resources for virtual machines, ensuring highly-efficient use of available hardware and complete isolation of virtual machine processes. Hypervisors (compute resources) can be organized into compute zones, which make it easy to offer tiered service levels and create private clouds for specific users. Each virtual machine in the cloud is hosted on a specific physical hypervisor (compute resource) server, from which it receives CPU, RAM, and storage capacity from the data stores attached to that hypervisor (compute resource). In this document, you can find information on how to manage hypervisors (compute resources). For more information on how to manage a specific hypervisor (compute resource), refer to Creating and managing hypervisors (compute resources). Hypervisors (compute resources) can run CentOS 7 and Virtuozzo Server 9. Note the following rules applicable to Virtuozzo Server 9 hypervisors (compute resources): Virtuozzo Server 9 and CentOS 7 hypervisors (compute resources) cannot reside in the same compute zone. Do not apply CentOS 7 backup servers to Virtuozzo Server 9 hypervisors (compute resources). Use only Virtuozzo Server 9 backup servers.

chunks.title: Creating and managing instance packages
chunks.content: Creating and managing instance packages Instance packages are preconfigured CPU/RAM/Disk/Bandwidth packages that can be selected during the virtual machine creation process. You can add multiple instance packages specifying different values for the parameters to suit your customer’s needs. Resources that are not set when creating an instance package (for example, swap disk size) are calculated automatically. Instance packages make it easier for users to create virtual machines. The users simply need to select one of the instance packages available to them in the wizard. However, it is still possible to set the virtual machine resources manually if required. Instance packages apply only to virtual machines created on KVM hypervisors (compute resources). To provide your users with the ability to choose virtual machine resources from the predefined instance package(s), add the necessary packages to the users’ bucket(s). After that, instance packages will appear in the virtual machine creation wizard, on the Resources step. Set up instance packages for cloud To enable your users to create virtual machines using instance packages, you need to perform the following configurations: Enable the instance packages permission. Add instance package(s) to your cloud. Add the instance package(s) to the users’ bucket. Interface configuration. Build virtual machine using instance packages.

chunks.title: Localization and customization
chunks.content: Localization and customization The search box in the Localization and Customization menu allows you to search by the following parameters: Item ID English Value Translation To search the Localization & Customization menu Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the i18n Customization icon. Click the required language name (for example, English). In the search box, type the search phrase and click the Search button (). If required, make changes and click Apply.

chunks.title: Assigning and unassigning IP address from a user
chunks.content: Assigning and unassigning IP address from a user You can assign and and unassign IP addresses to users from the network overview page. You can assign and unassign IP addresses from shared networks only. To assign an IP address to a user Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Networks icon. Click the name (label) of the network from which you wish to assign an IP address to a user. Click the Assign IP addresses button. On the window that pops up, select the following parameters: IP net - select from the drop-down list the IP net from which the IP address should be assigned. IP range - select from the drop-down list the IP range from which the IP address should be assigned. User - select from the drop-down list the user to whom you wish to assign IP addresses. Selection - type in the IP address you wish to assign and click Add. You can assign multiple IPs from the same form by filling in an address in the Selection field, clicking Add, and repeating the process for all the required IPs. You can assign a range of IPs by typing them in one of the following formats: 192.168.128.11-20, 192.168.128.11-192.168.128.20, or 192.168.128.11/30. If one or several IPs from the range are assigned to a different user or to VMs that do not belong to the required user, the IP range will not be assigned. The IP addresses and ranges that are to be assigned appear in the IP Addresses field.

chunks.title: Creating and managing IP nets
chunks.content: Creating and managing IP nets IP nets contain the IP address ranges of the network. You can add new IP nets to the network, edit and delete the existing nets, and add and edit IP ranges in the IP nets. For information on how to add IP ranges to IP nets, refer to IP ranges. You can add IP nets only to shared networks. To add an IP net to a network Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Networks icon. Click the label of the network to which you want to add an IP net. On the page that loads, click the New IP Net button. Fill in the details of the new IP net:Label - the name of the IP net. Network address - the network address of the IP net. Network mask - the network mask. Must be less or equal to 32. Default gateway - the default gateway to be added to the IP net automatically. Allow gateway to be outside from Ip Net - select the checkbox to allow the gateway to be outside from the IP net. Add default IP range - select the checkbox for the default IP range to be added to the IP net automatically. Otherwise, you’ll need to add the required IP ranges after the IP net is created. Click Submit to finish. To edit an IP net Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Networks icon. Click the label of the network which contains the IP net you wish to edit. Click the Actions button and select Edit next to the IP net you want to modify. Edit the details of the IP net:Label - the name of the IP net.

chunks.title: Creating and managing IP ranges
chunks.content: Creating and managing IP ranges IP ranges reside inside IP nets and include the IP addresses that are either assigned to a user or/and used by a VM. The IPs that are neither assigned to a user nor a VM are not shown in the IP range list but are available during VM creation. You can add new IP ranges and edit and delete the existing ones. To add IP ranges you first need to create a network and then add an IP net to that network. You can manage IP ranges only for shared networks. To add an IP range to an IP net Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Networks icon. Click the label of the network to which you want to add an IP net. Click the Actions button and select Add New IP Range next to the required IP net. Fill in the start and end address and the default gateway of the new IP range. Click Add to save the new IP range. The Add New IP Range button is not displayed if there are no IP addresses that can be added to the IP net. To edit an IP range in an IP net Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Networks icon. Click the label of the required network. Click the IP net in which you want to edit the IP range. Click the Actions button and select Edit next to the required IP range. Fill in the start and end address and the default gateway of the IP range. If you edit an IP range that includes used IPs, the edited range should include these IPs after the changes. Click Submit to save the changes.

chunks.title: Managing ISOs
chunks.content: Managing ISOs Virtuozzo allows uploading your custom bootable ISOs for recovery purposes. These could be different images for Windows/Linux/FreeBSD or any additional software. As a cloud administrator, you can limit user’s ability to upload and manage ISOs by permissions and in buckets. You can boot virtual machines from your own ISOs or the ISOs that are uploaded and made publicly available by other users. The default maximum size for uploading ISOs from the file system is 1 GB, this value can be changed via Control Panel > Admin > Settings > Configuration > Max upload size in bytes. There are no space limitations for the ISOs uploaded from the URL (except for your disk space limitations). As soon as you boot a VM from the installation ISO, Virtuozzo cannot control any VM components (backups, networks, disks). Be aware that all the contents of the disk might be deleted if a VM is booted from the ISO that installs a new distributive. If you boot a VM from an ISO with the RAM requirement larger than the VM’s RAM, the transaction will fail. If your cloud deployment is not a fresh installation, make sure that permissions on ISOs are enabled. For more info, refer to Permissions. You can upload your own ISOs and make them available to all users of the cloud (the way the templates work in Virtuozzo). After the ISO is uploaded, it is possible to select the Boot from ISO option on VM management screen.

chunks.title: Managing logs
chunks.content: Managing logs Virtuozzo logs all cloud management actions that take place on cloud resources, including virtual machines, disks, data stores, hypervisors (compute resources), templates, networks. View and manage logs In the Activity Log table, you can view and manage the log of all transactions in the cloud. To access and manage logs Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Logs menu. The Activity Log table provides the following details: Icon - indicates the status of an action. Ref - the number that you can click to view details of a specific transaction. Date - time when the action was performed. Action - the name of the transaction. Target - cloud resource with an identification number that you can click to view its details.You can view details on target cloud resources that are displayed in bold, indicating that they are available in the cloud. You cannot view details on resources that are unavailable, for example, resources that failed to be created. Dependent - the reference number of the previous transaction on which the current transaction depends. On the Logs page, you can click: Hide Successful Market Notifications to remove from the list actions that were performed successfully. Click this button again to show the full list. Complete, Running, Failed, or Cancelled to filter logs by their status. Failover Processes to view the list of failover logs. See Failover logs. Clean Logs to clear the logs completely.

chunks.title: Deliveries
chunks.content: Deliveries The Deliveries section shows all the notification deliveries in your cloud. If a subscription has a recipient list which contains multiple users, a separate delivery will be displayed for each of the recipients of the notification. You can delete notification data, including events, deliveries, and notifications for a particular period of time. To check notifications delivery Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Deliveries menu. You can view the deliveries in your system with the following details: Status - whether the notification was delivered. This status can indicate that the delivery is Complete, Running, or Failed. ID - the ID of the delivery. Subscription Name - the subscription within which this delivery was initiated. Click the label of the subscription to view its details. Recipient - the user to whom the notification is to be delivered. Destination - the destination to which the notification was delivered: SMTP or SENDMAIL for email notifications and INTERNAL for notifications in CP. Date - the time when the notification was sent. To delete notification data Run the following command from the onapp user: cd /onapp/interface RAILS_ENV=production rake messaging:clean_notification_elements[2016-09-20,2016-09-23]Copy cd /onapp/interface RAILS_ENV=production rake messaging:clean_notification_elements[2016-09-20,2016-09-23] Change the dates in the example above to the ones you require and separate them by comma.

chunks.title: Events
chunks.content: Events The Events page shows the events which occurred and which users were notified. Virtuozzo currently offers two event types: system and custom. You can view a list of all event types, view system events, and create, trigger, edit, and delete custom events. To view a list of events Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Events menu. The page that loads shows the list of events which have occurred in the system with their details: Date - the time and date when the event occurred. Event Type - the type of the event. Data - the text of the notification that was sent about the event. To view a list of system event types System events cannot be edited or deleted. Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Event Types menu. Go to the System Event Types tab. The page that loads shows the list of system event types registered in system with their details: ID - the ID of the event. Event type - the type of the event. To add a custom event type Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Event Types menu. Go to the Custom Event types tab. Click the Create New Event Type button. On the page that loads, enter the name and description of your custom event type. Click Submit to save the new event type. To trigger a custom event If required, you can trigger the event from the list of custom events manually. When you trigger a custom event type, a new popup window appears where you can enter the text of the message to be passed into the notification template.

chunks.title: Creating and managing gateways
chunks.content: Creating and managing gateways The Gateways section lets you create gateways for your notification system. Gateways are used when setting up a subscription and determine in what way users will be contacted: via email or internal notifications in CP. You can create multiple gateways to verify without any limitation. To view your gateways Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Gateways menu. The following page shows your gateways with their names and the types: SMTP SENDMAIL INTERNAL To create a gateway Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Gateways menu. Click the Add button () or the New gateway button. On the page that appears, select the delivery method for the gateway: SMTP or SENDMAIL for email notifications INTERNAL for internal notifications in the CP Click Select to proceed to the next gateway creation step. Depending on the selected delivery method, fill in the following details: For the Transaction Approvals functionality, you need to add a SENDMAIL gateway with the System SENDMAIL Gateway label or/and an SMTP gateway with the System SMTP Gateway label. The SENDMAIL delivery method Name - the name for your new gateway. The name of the gateway should not contain any special characters. Primary - move the slider to the right to mark current gateway as primary to be used to receive the notifications on set/reset/forgot password/unlock a user. The previous primary gateway will be unmarked. From - the email address from which emails will be sent.

chunks.title: Notifications and notification system elements
chunks.content: Notifications and notification system elements The Control Panel’s Notification menu lets you configure the notifications for your CP. You can select the events about which to notify your users. Manage notifications To configure notifications, you need to: Enable notifications for your cloud - the configured subscriptions will send notifications only if you enable this option. Configure gateways - select what type of notifications you want to send: SMTP/SENDMAIL emails or internal notifications in CP. Add notification templates - notification templates determine the text of the messages your users will receive. Add custom events - you can add custom events to send notifications when you require. Create recipients lists - recipients lists include users whom you want to address certain notifications. Set up subscriptions - a subscription ties all your configurations together. After you set up subscriptions your users will start receiving notifications. After these configurations, you can: Check whether your notifications have been delivered - you can check whether the sent notifications have been delivered successfully. View internal notifications in Control Panel - you can view internal notifications in your Control Panel. You need to have messaging permissions enabled to configure notifications. For more information, refer to Permissions.

chunks.title: Creating and managing notification templates
chunks.content: Creating and managing notification templates The Notification Templates section lets you create message texts that will be sent to your users via email or internal notifications in CP. Notification templates are used when setting up a subscription for your users. There are two types of notification templates: system templates that come pre-installed with Virtuozzo and cannot be deleted but only edited, and custom templates which you add to your cloud. Notification templates include message texts that will be sent to your users via email or internal notifications in CP. There are two types of notification templates: system templates that come pre-installed with Virtuozzo and cannot be deleted but only edited, and custom templates which you add to your cloud. To view your notification templates Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Notification Templates menu. The page that loads shows your notification templates with their names, indicators whether this is a system or a custom template and the template’s text. If a template contains a long message, only the beginning of the text will be displayed. To add a notification template Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Notification Templates menu. Click the Add button () or the New notification template button in the lower-right corner. On the page that loads, fill in the label and the text of the template. The label of the template should not contain any special characters.

chunks.title: Creating and managing subscriptions
chunks.content: Creating and managing subscriptions Using the Subscriptions section you determine who of your users are notified about which events. A subscription is the final step of a notifications configuration which ties together a recipients list, a gateway and a notification template. Subscriptions determine who of your users are notified about which events and the type of the notification: email or internal notification in CP. To view a list of subscriptions and their details Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Subscriptions menu. On the following page, you can view subscriptions and their details:Name - the label of the subscription. Event Type - the event type with which the subscription is associated. Template - the subscription’s notification template. Click the template to view its details. Gateways - the name of the gateway and the means by which the notifications will be sent. Click the gateway to view its details. Recipients Lists - the subscription’s recipients list. Click the label of the recipients list to view the list of users in it and their emails. Additionally, you can click the name of the desired subscription to view the gateways, recipients lists, events, and templates associated with it. To add a subscription Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Subscriptions menu. Click the Add button () or the New Subscription button. On the page that loads, fill in the following details:Name - the label for the subscription.

chunks.title: Managing compute zone networks
chunks.content: Managing compute zone networks Networks can easily be attached and removed from compute zones. This association between a compute zone and a network is called a network join. If the compute zone loses network connection, a warning message All compute resources are not responsive will be displayed. You can add networks to a compute zone only if the network belongs to a network zone of the same type as the compute zone. For more information, refer to Zone types. To remove a compute zone network Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Compute Zones icon. Click the label of the compute zone you want to manage networks for. Click the Tools button, and then select Manage Networks. Click the Detach Network button () next to the desired compute zone network. In the dialog, click OK. To add a compute zone network Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Compute Zones icon. Click the label of the compute zone you want to manage networks for. Click the Tools button and select Manage Networks. In the Attach Network section, fill in the following:Interface - enter its interface name (eth0, eth1). Network - in the drop-down list, choose the desired network. Click the Add Network button in the lower-right corner.

chunks.title: Creating and managing network zones
chunks.content: Creating and managing network zones Network zones can be used to create different tiers of service–for example, by setting up different zones for different network resources. Network zones have types which are inherited by the networks in the zone. Later networks can be attached to a hypervisor (compute resource)/compute zone of the same type. Networks can be moved from one network zone to another, but the zones should be of the same type. For more information, refer to Zone types. The table below demonstrates the available network zone types for different networks: Network type Network zone type vCloud Director VPC Other Virtual You can create new network zones, view existing network zones and its details, edit network zones as well as add and remove networks from network zone. For more information on network settings, refer to Networking. To create a network zone Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. On the page that appears, click the Network Zones icon. On the following page, click the Create Network Zone button () or the Create Network Zone button in the lower-right corner. On the screen that appears, fill in the following:Label - enter the name of the network zone. Server type - choose the server type from the drop-down list:virtual - applies to for a KVM zone.The zone’s type cannot be changed after the zone is created. Location group - from the drop-down list, select the location group to assign the network zone.

chunks.title: Creating and managing recipes
chunks.content: Creating and managing recipes The recipe is the plugin mechanism used for adding new functionalities to the cloud. Each recipe is a set of instructions that trigger events at certain stages during the execution of certain services/event in the cloud. Essentially, recipes allow inputting code into virtual machines, appliances or the Control Panel server. This enables administrators to use recipes for configuring the server or report on it, thus providing advanced customization options in a standard environment. Recipes run over SSH, and all commands triggered can run on virtual machines, appliances or the Control Panel server. SSH connection is not required for running recipes on VMware virtual machines. Recipes can range from very simple actions to complex multi step automations interacting with other internal and external systems. Virtuozzo OnApp Support will not be able to create custom recipes based on your requirements, or troubleshoot/debug the lines of code within your own recipes via our support channels. If you would like to commission your own recipes but don’t have resources to do it internally, please contact your account manager for a custom quote. Control Panel does not update the status of the recipe if it takes longer than 1 hour to complete the transaction. Recipe use Recipes allow admins to perform the following operations: Perform post script installation. Use post provision installation scripts for third-party applications, agents, etc. Disk reclaiming.

chunks.title: Creating and managing recipe groups
chunks.content: Creating and managing recipe groups Recipe groups allow Virtuozzo OnApp administrators to organize individual recipes into groups that can be used as a bucket resource. This allows you to easily create groups of recipes which can be added to the bucket to limit the recipes that are available to a user. The recipe groups have hierarchical (tree) structure: Recipe group Child group Recipes You can also add a recipe directly to the recipe group section without assigning it to a child group. Click the recipe group’s label to expand the list of child groups, then click the recipe group’s label to view the list of recipes, respectively. To add a recipe group Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Recipes > Recipe Groups menu. On the page that follows, click the Add button () in the upper-right corner or the Create New Recipe Group button in the lower-right corner. Give a name to your group. Click Save. On the page that appears, you’ll be prompted to assign a recipe to a group. To add a child group to a recipe group Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Recipes > Recipe Groups menu. Click next to the required group’s label, then select Add Child. Give a name to your child group. Click the Save button to confirm. To assign a recipe to a recipe group Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Recipes > Recipe Groups menu. Click next to the required group’s or child group’s label, then select Add Recipe. Choose the required recipe from the drop-down menu. Click the Save button to confirm.

chunks.title: Managing virtual machine recovery points
chunks.content: Managing virtual machine recovery points Please note that the Recovery Points functionality is experimental. Recovery points are created as a result of virtual machine data replication on a third-party backup service. Integration with the backup service is handled by means of a plugin that you can install to your Control Panel. The recovery point represents a point-in-time full backup from which you can restore a virtual machine. In Control Panel, recovery points become available after you: Attach a backup resource to a virtual machine. Create an auto backup preset and the preset runs according to a schedule. You can also create a recovery point manually after you complete the preceding steps. In this document, you can find information on how to create and manage recovery points for a virtual machine. For the R1Soft backup plugin, you can set the total amount of recovery points that will be created for a virtual machine by the Max recovery points option while creating an auto backup preset. After the maximum limit is reached, new recovery points overwrite the existing ones. For the Veeam backup plugin, you use Retention Policy in Veeam Backup & Replication UI to control the number of recovery points that are retained on a disk. After the specified number of recovery points is exceeded, the earliest recovery points are automatically deleted to retain the new ones. The Recovery Points-related permissions are disabled by default for the User role.

chunks.title: Template stores
chunks.content: Template stores Template store enables you to organize individual templates into groups that can be used as a paid resource for buckets. This allows you to easily create groups of templates which can be added to the bucket to limit the amount or types of templates that are available to a user. Also you can add ISO and OVA templates to the template store and set prices for these templates in the bucket. After ISO or OVA template is added to the template store, you can create a VM using this template. Prices for templates are set in the bucket’s Rate Card. For more information, refer to Configuring resource allocation and prices. Manage template groups The template groups have a hierarchical (tree) structure: Template group (for example, OS) Child group Templates Click the Template group’s label to expand the list of child groups, then click the template group’s label to view the list of templates, respectively. To add a template group Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Templates > Template Store menu. Click the Add button () or the Create New Template Group button in lower-right corner. On the page that appears, fill in the following: Label - specify the name of your group. Specify the Windows Licensing type: MAK, KMS, or User license. For KMS licensing, set the following parameters:Server Label – the name of the KMS server. KMS Server Host – the hostname of the licensing server. KMS Server Port – the port used to connect to the licensing server. Click Save.

chunks.title: Managing my template groups
chunks.content: Managing my template groups My Template Groups allow you to create own license groups for your own personal/custom templates. The groups cannot be shared amongst the users. Also, for Windows-based templates, My Template Groups provide the possibility to use your own licensing type regardless of your bucket. For your convenience, the My Template Groups menu has a hierarchical (tree) structure: Template group (for example, OS) Child group Templates You may assign templates directly to the group, or create a child group(s) and assign templates there. To add a template group Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Templates > My Template Groups menu. On the following page, click the Add button () or the Create New My Template Group button in the lower-right corner. On the page that appears, fill in the following: Label - specify the name of your group. If you are planning to use this group for Windows templates, specify the Windows Licensing type: MAK , KMS , or Own (user license).This licensing type will apply to all templates directly in the group and in the child groups. For KMS licensing, set the following parameters:Server Label – the name of the KMS server. KMS Server Host – the hostname of the licensing server. KMS Server Port – the port used to connect to the licensing server. Click Save. On the page that appears, you can add a template or a child to the group, edit the group, or delete it.

chunks.title: Sysadmin
chunks.content: Sysadmin The Sysadmin page provides statistics and tools for a number of system administration tasks. These tools are divided into the following tabs: Sysadmin tools Services Application errors Activity log Control Panel maintenance IP usage report Resource diffs Sysadmin tools Background task daemon Daemon is responsible for executing all background tasks such as: Transactions Backup takers Billing stats updater Cluster monitor Hypervisor (compute resource) monitor Schedule runner To operate the daemon, use the following buttons: Reload daemon – restarts the tasks, and completes all running tasks if their PIDs still exist. Stop daemon - completes any backups in progress, but prevents any more backups from starting; stops all tasks in progress. Start daemon - starts up all the tasks. Check status – shows the PID of the task and its status. Availability check Availability check enables one to see the status of Services monitoring tool and perform the following functions: Reload the Virtuozzo OnApp Services Monitoring Tool. Disable the Virtuozzo OnApp Services Monitoring Tool. Enable the Virtuozzo OnApp Services Monitoring Tool. Check status of the Virtuozzo OnApp Services Monitoring Tool. CDN API CDN API checks API for accessibility and an allocated CdnCloudRef. CDN Sync Runner CDN Sync Runner checks CDN for accessibility, as well as for errors and warnings. CDN is an experimental feature.

chunks.title: Configuring resource allocation and prices
chunks.content: Configuring resource allocation and prices Buckets enable you to set up resource allocation and pricing separately. They are subdivided into two tabs: Access Control - in this section you configure the resource allocation for the users under this bucket. If you assign a bucket to a user, that user will have access only to those resources which you have added to the bucket. If no resources are added to a section of the Access Control, e.g. compute zones, the user under the bucket will not have access to any of your compute zones. Rate Card - in this section you set up prices for the resources and the amount of resources users can request for free. Users under the bucket will be billed according to the prices you configure in the Rate Card. These tabs are further subdivided into sections that depend on the server types of resources: Virtual - the server type under which KVM compute, data store, network, and backup server zones of the virtual machine type can be created. Other - the resources that relate to the system and do not have a server type. This section includes backup resource zones, template stores, edge groups, recipe groups, and service add-on groups. For convenience, you can duplicate resources from the Access Control to the Rate Card and vice versa. When adding a resource to the Access Control, select the Duplicate to rate card checkbox, and the resource will be added to the Rate Card with no prices and free limits by default.

chunks.title: Restrictions sets
chunks.content: Restrictions sets The restrictions set is a customizable group of limitations. Configure restrictions sets to create a subadmin role, with control over a limited amount of cloud resources. This tool gives cloud administrators more flexibility in limiting resources and operations available to subadmin role(s). Creating a new restrictions set associates a role or number of roles with certain resources’ limitations. The subadmins can only view and control the part of cloud assigned to them by the cloud administrator. Within that part they have admin permissions. However, they cannot view or use the resources of the whole cloud. Previously, the exact list of resources and actions that the users were able to handle in their cloud was defined by the following parameters: Bucket - configures which resources are available to users (for example, data store zones, recipes, network zones, and so on). If none are added, the user will have unlimited resources. Roles/permissions - specifies which actions the user can perform with those resources configured by the bucket (for example, See all data store zones in the cloud, Edit own recipes only, etc.). The restrictions sets add the possibility to tie the user limitations with the user groups. With this new option, you can choose if the particular resources are restricted by the following: Bucket resources - if restricted by buckets, the subadmins will be able to manage only those resources which are added to a bucket.

chunks.title: Creating and managing roles
chunks.content: Creating and managing roles Virtuozzo allows you to assign roles to users. Each role has a set of permissions associated with it. By assigning users to different roles you can control what those users are allowed to do. To view the roles list, go to the Control Panel’s Roles menu. You will get the list of roles together with their labels, amount of assigned users, and actions, which you can perform with the role (edit, delete, and clone). Roles are assigned to users during the user creation process. Virtuozzo,provides the following pre-configured user roles: Administrator User In this chapter: Creating and configuring roles Creating and deleting super admin role Managing transaction approvals

chunks.title: Managing Identity Providers
chunks.content: Managing Identity Providers This page provides procedures for viewing and editing Identity Providers To view a list of Identity Providers Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Authentication icon. You will see all SAML IdPs available in your cloud with their key details:Name - the name of the Identity Provider. IdP SSO Target Url - the URL to which the authentication request is sent. Status - either active or disabled. Actions - click the button to edit, delete or access metadata of this Identity Provider. To see more detailed description of the Identity Provider, click its label. To enable or disable IdP, go to the Edit screen. To edit an Identity Provider instance Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Authentication icon. Click the Actions button next to the Identity Provider you want to edit and select Edit. Fill in the following: Idp sso target url and Idp cert are given by the Identity Provider. Idp cert fingerprint will be calculated by the system. Enabled - move the slider to the right to enable this identity provider at the login screen. Show on login page – move the slider to the right to show a SAML provider on the login page. Name - enter the name of the identity provider. Icon - select the icon file, which will be displayed on the login page. Issuer - the name of the service provider; by default - the address of your Control Panel. Idp sso target url - the URL to which the login authentication request should be sent.

chunks.title: Schedule settings
chunks.content: Schedule settings The schedules settings screen provides an overview of all virtual machines’ backup schedules. This section provides information on how you can create, view, edit, and delete backup schedules. Create schedules When you create a schedule, you can set the time when the backup will be taken. Each backup erases the previous backup and a new backup is not scheduled if another auto-backup from the same schedule is pending or running. When a schedule is no longer needed, we recommend deleting it so that the task will no longer run. Manage schedules You can view, edit, and delete a schedule. To view schedules Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Schedules icon to see a list of all schedules on the system along with their details:Date - the time when the schedule was created. Target - the machine for which the schedule was created. Action - the scheduled action. Period - how frequently the backup will occur according to a period type set in the next step.For example, if you set 2 as a period and days as a period type, the backup will take place at the same time every two days. By default, this field is set to 1. Period type - the backup period: days, weeks, months, or years. Rotation period - the number of backups, after which the first backup will be deleted.By default, this field is set to 1 . It means that the old backup is deleted after a new backup occurs. If you set 2 in this field, it means that the first backup will be deleted next one.

chunks.title: Creating and managing service add-ons
chunks.content: Creating and managing service add-ons This chapter provides an overview of service add-ons, the management tips, the information on creating your own service add-ons and providing them as a paid resource for your customers. The Service Add-ons functionality allows you to present to your customers additional services on top of your current IaaS virtual machine offering. You can offer features such as Managed Services, Software Installations and components currently not integrated in Virtuozzo Server. Types of service add-ons There are three types of service add-ons - virtual machine, system and user service add-ons. A virtual machine service add-on can be optionally assigned to a virtual machine or removed from it by users upon their desire to use or not the specific extra resources you offer. A system service add-on provides the ability for you to add obligatory services to a virtual machine, template, or OVA, which cannot be removed by an end user. As for a user service add-on, the services are applied to a user that can be run in Control Panel. Create and configure a service add-on Below is the service add-on creation and configuration workflow. To create a service add-on Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Service Add-ons > Service Add-ons menu. On the following page, click the Add button () in the upper-right corner or the Create New Service Add-on button in the lower-right corner. On the page that appears, fill in the following: Label – give your service add-on a name.

chunks.title: Managing a service add-on store
chunks.content: Managing a service add-on store Service add-on store enables you to organize individual service add-ons into groups that can be used as a paid resource for buckets. It allows you to easily create groups that can be added to a bucket to limit the amount or types of service add-ons available to a user. Ensure the Service Add-on Groups permissions are on before managing a service add-on store. For more information about permissions, refer to Permissions. Service add-on groups The service add-on groups have a hierarchical (tree) structure: Service add-on group Child group Service add-ons Click the service add-on group label to expand a list of child groups, then click the service add-on group label to view a list of service add-ons. To add a service add-on group Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Service Add-ons > Store menu. On the page that appears, click the Add button () in the upper-right corner or the Create New Group button in the lower-right corner and fill in the following:Label - give a name to your group. Icon - upload the service add-on group icon (click Choose File to select the necessary image). Click Save. To add a child service add-on group to your service add-on group, click next to your service add-on group and select Add Child. To assign a service add-on to a service add-on group Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Service Add-ons > Store menu. Click next to the required child group label, then select Add Service Add-on.

chunks.title: Managing templates
chunks.content: Managing templates You can perform a set of actions with the templates: View, edit, and delete system templates. Create, edit, delete, and make public custom templates. Manage template recipes and recipe variables. Manage template system service add-ons. Download new and update existing templates. Use Virtuozzo Server templates to build virtual machines only on Virtuozzo Server hypervisors (compute resources). You can keep using legacy templates in legacy compute zones. View template details The Control Panel’s Templates List menu lists all of the templates available on your system, their version number, the number of recipes assigned to the template, the Operating System they install, whether swap disk is allowed, whether you can adjust their CPU cores/priority & RAM without rebooting a virtual machine based on that template (“resize without reboot”), and whether hot migration is allowed. The templates are organized into five tabs: All templates - a list of available and installed templates. System templates - the OS images provided by Virtuozzo. My templates - the list of custom templates created by the user who is currently logged in. User templates - the list of templates converted by all users in the cloud from VM backups. To see user templates, make sure the See User Templates permission is enabled. Inactive - the templates that are currently unavailable to build VM on.

chunks.title: Creating and managing templates
chunks.content: Creating and managing templates This chapter provides an overview on what templates in Virtuozzo are, the management tips, the information on creating your own templates and providing them as a paid resource for your customers. What are templates? A template is a fully preconfigured operating system environment – a tar + gzip archive that contains the root directory of an operating system. A basic template includes the data needed for a minimum OS installation, but templates may also include applications and additional OS components. Virtuozzo templates are used to deploy virtual machines. The Virtuozzo template library includes over 100 VM templates based on various 32-bit and 64-bit versions of Windows and Linux operating systems. Windows templates To create a virtual machine from a template based on paid software, such as MS Windows, you must have a valid license. The system verifies if you have a license before allowing the VM to be created, so before creating a VM you must first upload the license keys you’ve bought to Virtuozzo, or connect to a licensing server. Virtuozzo supports three license types: MAK licensing: the default licensing type applied to all Windows-based VMs. KMS licensing: this is applicable to Windows 2008 and up. User licenses: allow end users to input a license key when creating a VM. For more information, refer to Managing template software licenses. Types of templates There are two different kinds of templates: System templates.

chunks.title: Managing the look&feel of Control Panel
chunks.content: Managing the look&feel of Control Panel You can change the look of your Control Panel in several ways: Using Look & Feel UI options. Adding your custom CSS rules. Adding your custom Java Scripts. Please be aware that Virtuozzo supports the following: Two latest versions of the most popular browsers are supported (Google Chrome and Firefox). Opera is not supported. JavaScript must be enabled in the browser. Theme You can manage various aspects of the Control Panel’s look & feel, including the logo displayed, background colors, and other graphics, and thus receive a unique theme. To create a custom theme Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Look & Feel icon. On the following page, click the Add button (). Fill in the following: Theme options Label – give a name to your theme. Active – move the slider to specify whether the theme is displayed or not. If this option is enabled, the default colors and graphics are used, irrespective of other settings. User Group User groups - select the groups of users for whom you wish to apply the theme. General Title - enter the title which will be displayed at the top left corner of the browser window. Logo - click the Choose File button to choose a custom logo.Move the Disable Logo slider to the right to prevent a logo from displaying (no logo will be displayed). Logo mini - click the Choose File button to choose a custom logo mini.

chunks.title: Managing virtual machine transactions and logs
chunks.content: Managing virtual machine transactions and logs The system records a detailed log of all the transactions taking place on your virtual machines. The list of transactions logged by the system includes: Provision virtual server Startup virtual server Stop virtual server Resize virtual server without reboot Configure Operating System Build disk Resize disk Format disk Destroy disk Take backup Convert backup Restore backup Destroy backups Destroy virtual server Destroy template Download template Update firewall You can view virtual machine transactions, cancel pending tasks, and cancel a TakeBackup transaction running longer and exceeding the time for a zombie transaction. To view transactions for a virtual machine Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Virtual Servers menu. Click the label of the virtual machine you’re interested in. The details screen for that virtual machine shows recent transactions in the Activity Log section. To cancel all pending tasks Click the Cancel All Pending Tasks for this virtual server button. To cancel a TakeBackup transaction running longer and exceeding the time set for a zombie transaction Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Virtual Servers menu. Click the label of the required virtual machine. On the following page, in the Activity Log section, hover over the icon of the transaction and then click that appears on the icon of this transaction.

chunks.title: User accounts
chunks.content: User accounts There are two types of accounts in Virtuozzo: administrators and users. An administrator account is created automatically when Virtuozzo is installed. Administrators have full access to the system, including managing virtual machines and hypervisors (compute resources), performing actions on templates and backups, and configuring data stores and networks. There can be several administrators in Virtuozzo. Create and manage user accounts User accounts are created by administrators and have access to those actions which are specified by an administrator. To add a new user Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Users menu. Click the Add button () or the Create User button in the lower-right corner. Fill in the user creation form:Move the Use Gravatar slider to the right to use the gravatar image. Login name - provide user login name. It can consist of 2-40 characters, letters [A-Za-z], digits [0-9], dash [ - ], lower dash [ _ ], [@]. You can use both lower- and uppercase letters. The dash [ - ] and [@] symbols are not allowed as first characters of the login name. First name - specify the user’s first name. It can consist of any 1-20 characters. Last name - specify the user’s last name. It can consist of any 1-20 characters. Email address - specify the user’s email. Time zone - select the required time zone from the drop-down box. Locale - specify user locale settings by selecting the appropriate locale from the drop-down list (see Locales).

chunks.title: Creating and managing user groups
chunks.content: Creating and managing user groups You can assign users to different user groups. At present, you can configure the following for user groups: Assign a UI theme to specific user groups (Admin > Settings > Look&Feel) Set the default roles Specify buckets To view user group details Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Groups menu. On the following page, click the label of the required user group to view the following parameters: Roles - roles available to the users within this user group. Assigned User IPs - click the number next to it to view the list of IP addresses assigned to users within this user group with the following details:IP - the IP address. User - the name of the user. Assigned at - the date and time when the IP address was assigned to the user. Virtual Server IPs - click the number next to it to view the list of IP addresses assigned to all the virtual machines of users within this user group with the following details:IP - the IP address. Virtual server - the IP address assigned to the virtual machine. User - the name of the virtual machine’s owner. Assigned at - the date and time when the IP address was assigned to the virtual machine. Bucket - the bucket used by the users within this user group. User Buckets - buckets available for assignment to the users within this user group. To create a user group Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Groups menu. On the page that follows, click the Add button () or the Create Group button in the lower-right corner.

chunks.title: Managing virtual machine advanced configuration
chunks.content: Managing virtual machine advanced configuration You can manage your virtual machines at a raw configuration level by editing the XML configuration file available for each VM in your Control Panel. The functionality is available for virtual machines that are built on KVM hypervisors (compute resources). Virtual machines with modified XML configuration are not supported by the Virtuozzo Support Team. Manage virtual machine advanced configuration You can enable advanced configuration and edit XML configuration for virtual machines To enable advanced configuration Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click Configuration icon. Go to the Defaults tab. Move the Allow advanced VS management slider to the right. Click the Save Configuration button. Please note that the system will restart Virtuozzo services automatically after you save the new configuration. To edit XML configuration Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Virtual Servers menu. Click the label of the desired virtual machine. Click the Actions button, point to Options , then select Edit XML Config . Click the Unlock button to be able to edit the XML file. In the pop-up box, click Yes to confirm your action. Edit the configuration and click the Save button to apply changes. In the pop-up box, select whether you want to save changes with or without a reboot.To revert changes that you made before saving the configuration, click the Cancel button.

chunks.title: Managing virtual machine backup schedules
chunks.content: Managing virtual machine backup schedules The schedules screen lists the virtual machines’ scheduled backups. In this document, you can find information on how to manage virtual machine backup schedules. To view virtual machine incremental backup schedules Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Virtual Servers menu. Click the label of the virtual machine you’re interested in. Go to the Backups > Schedules tab or click Auto-backups under the Options section to view incremental backup schedules only. On the screen that appears, you will see the list of backup schedules along with their details:Date - the time when the schedule was created. Target - the machine or disk for which the schedule was created (depending on the backup type). Action - the scheduled action. Period - how frequently the backup will occur according to a period type set in the next step.For example, if you set 2 as a period and days as a period type, the backup will take place at the same time every two days. By default, this field is set to 1. Period type - the backup period: days, weeks, months, or years. Rotation period - the number of backups, after which the first backup will be deleted.By default, this field is set to 1, so it means that the old one backup is deleted after a new backup occurs. If you set 2 in this field, the first backup will be deleted next but one. If you set 4, three most recent backups and the new one will be stored, while the initial one will be deleted.

chunks.title: Managing virtual machine integrated console
chunks.content: Managing virtual machine integrated console Virtuozzo provides an integrated VNC console that gives users direct access to virtual machines through the Control Panel UI. The noVNC console is provided for virtual machines built on KVM based on WebSockets. Users with the Administrator role can access all virtual machine consoles for support and troubleshooting purposes. The console connects a user browser to a VNC port or VNC WebSocket port available via a hypervisor (compute resource) for the guest console. To access a VNC console of a virtual machine via Control Panel Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Virtual Servers menu. Click the label of the destination virtual machine. Go to the Console tab. OR Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Virtual Servers menu. Click the Actions button next to the destination virtual machine and select Console. For an HTML5 console, click the Re-connect button if the connection is lost. The re-connection to the console runs as follows: If the console runs as expected, clicking the Re-connect button causes disconnection and the console is re-connected automatically after 1.5 seconds. If the console gets stuck, clicking the Re-connect button runs your request once again and re-connects the console without reloading. If the console gets disconnected with a status code and an error message, the console is re-connected automatically after 1.5 seconds.

chunks.title: Managing virtual machine power options
chunks.content: Managing virtual machine power options Virtual machine power options include a list of actions you can run to change a VM power status. You can manage power options for a specific virtual machine or power on/off multiple VMs that reside on the same hypervisor (compute resource). To reboot a virtual machine Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Virtual Servers menu. Click the label of the required virtual machine. Click the Actions button, point to Power , and select Reboot Virtual Server. Click the OK button in the pop-up box to confirm the reboot. To reboot in recovery Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Virtual Servers menu. Click the label of the required virtual machine. Click the Actions button, point to Power, and select Reboot in Recovery . Click the Yes button in the pop-up box to confirm the reboot in the recovery mode. For VMs with password encryption enabled, the temporary login is root and the password is recovery. For VMs with password encryption disabled, the “root” password will be used to reboot the VM in recovery. Windows virtual machines boot from the Linux-based recovery template in the recovery mode. You need to log in as admin via SSH or VNC console and mount a Windows system disk manually. You cannot work with the “whole” disk (like mount -t ntfs-3g /dev/sdb1) while mounting and checking block devices inside the recovery image as the Windows disk is split into partitions. To suspend a virtual machine Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Virtual Servers menu.

chunks.title: Viewing virtual machine statistics
chunks.content: Viewing virtual machine statistics For your convenience, the system tracks VM performance and generates statistics on CPU utilization, billing, network interface usage, and disk IOPS. In this document, you can find information on how to view virtual machine statistics. Virtual machine CPU utilization Virtuozzo tracks CPU usage for virtual machines and generates charts that help analyze VM performance. The charts show the total CPU usage for all the cores of this particular VM for a specified time period. The vertical axis shows the CPU usage percentage (CPU percentage is the core-independent quantity). The horizontal axis defines a time period. To view CPU usage statistics Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Virtual Servers menu. Click the label of the virtual machine you’re interested in. Go to the Overview > CPU Usage tab. On the screen that appears, the top chart shows CPU usage for the last 24 hours. The bottom chart shows usage for the last three months (if there is enough data). If there is less data available, the chart will show utilization for the time available. Move the Show in My Timezone slider to the right if you want to show bandwidth statistics according to your profile’s timezone settings. To zoom into a time period, click and drag in a chart. Click the Reset Zoom button to zoom out again. You can filter the statistics by date and time - select the time period from the drop-down menu and click the Apply button.

chunks.title: Creating data stores
chunks.content: Creating data stores Data stores provide disk space for your virtual servers and operating systems. Data stores are attached to hypervisors (compute resources). Data stores have types they inherit from the zone to which they belong. Later, data stores can be attached to a hypervisor (compute resource)/compute zone with the same type. Data stores can be moved from one data store zone to another, but the zones should have the same type. For more information, refer to Zone types. Use caution when changing data store settings. Data stores provide disk space for your virtual servers and operating systems. Data stores are attached to hypervisors (compute resources). After successfully installing the Control Panel server and hypervisors (compute resources), follow the procedure to set up a data store. To create a QCOW2 data store Go to your Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the Data Stores icon. Click the Create Data Store button in the lower-right corner and fill in the following: Step 1 of 2. Properties Label - enter the data store label. Data store type - select qcow2. Enabled - move the slider to the right to turn on the data store. If disabled, new disks are forbidden to be created automatically on the data store. It prevents the data store from becoming too full and the automatic creation of root disks on particular data stores (high speed, etc.). Click Next. Step 2 of 2.

chunks.title: Installing templates
chunks.content: Installing templates One of the main prerequisites for creating a virtual machine is installing a template, creating a template group, and assigning the template to the template group. To download and install a template from a remote template server Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Templates > Template List menu. Go to the System Templates tab. The page that loads will list the installed templates. On the Available tab, you can view a list of templates available for installation. In the Search box, select the checkbox next to the desired filter option to filter the templates by operating system, virtualization, architecture, and the availability of guest agents. Click next to the desired template to install. Downloading a template may take some time. For more information on installing templates, see Creating and installing templates. To add a template group Go to your Control Panel > Cloud > Templates > Template Store menu. Click the Add button () or the Create New Template Group button in lower-right corner. On the page that appears, fill in the following:For more details about template software licenses, refer to Managing template software licenses Label - specify the name of your group. Specify the Windows Licensing type: MAK, KMS, or User license. For KMS licensing, set the following parameters:Server Label – the name of the KMS server. KMS Server Host – the hostname of the licensing server. KMS Server Port – the port used to connect to the licensing server. Click Save.

chunks.title: Managing Storage licenses
chunks.content: Managing Storage licenses This page describes the process of managing Storage licenses. You will learn to do the following: Install a new license for a Storage cluster. Update the installed license. View the installed license contents. Check the current license status. Obtain the hardware node ID The hardware node ID (HWID) is required to purchase a Storage license. You can obtain the HWID with the vstorage stat --license-hwid command. For example: # vstorage -c stor1 stat --license-hwid ... 3F96.DFF2.EAF6.CE86.DD49.786C.DC01.3D53Copy # vstorage -c stor1 stat --license-hwid ... 3F96.DFF2.EAF6.CE86.DD49.786C.DC01.3D53 A Storage hardware node ID is not the same as a Virtuozzo hardware node ID shown by the vzlicview command. Install the license Along with installing Virtuozzo licenses on all clients in a cluster, you need to install a separate license to start using the Storage functionality. One license is required per cluster. You can install the license from any server participating in the cluster: an MDS server, a chunk server, or a client.

Thus, all the functionality coming from vstorage-ui-agent is not available. This version does not support the prepare_vstorage_drive script. To install a Storage cluster Install Storage packages: yum groupinstall vstorageCopy yum groupinstall vstorage Specify MDS server discovery. To specify the IP address of an MDS server manually, create a bs.list file in the /etc/vstorage/clusters/Cluster_Name directory (create this directory if it does not exist) on the server you are configuring for the cluster and indicate the IP address and port for connecting to the MDS server. Use the IP address intended for a Storage network. echo "10.200.200.11:2510" >> /etc/vstorage/clusters/Cluster_Name/bs.

chunks.title: Extending your license
chunks.content: Extending your license To upgrade from Virtuozzo OnApp to Virtuozzo Server 9, we will need to extend the feature set of your current Control Panel license key. It is completely free and does not require any changes in your contract. To do that: Go to your Virtuozzo OnApp 7 Control Panel > Admin > Settings menu. Click the License icon. In the License Key field, you will find the key in the “XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX” format. Send the Virtuozzo Billing Team an email specifying your Control Panel license key and the number of hypervisors in your infrastructure. You can find the email address of the Virtuozzo Billing Team on every invoice you receive from Virtuozzo. If you are unsure, don’t hesitate to contact your account manager. Below is an email example: Hello Virtuozzo Billing Team, I am in the process of upgrading to Virtuozzo Server 9. My Control Panel license key is XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX. I have ten hypervisors in my infrastructure. In response, you will receive confirmation that the Control Panel license key has been upgraded to support Virtuozzo Server 9 compute zones and a number of activation keys for the upgraded hypervisors. With this, you can proceed to the next upgrade step—upgrading Control Panel from CentOS 7 to Virtuozzo Server 9.

chunks.title: Upgrading Control Panel
chunks.content: Upgrading Control Panel Prerequisites Upgrade your Control Panel (with the name source-CP) to the latest 7.0 version. Deploy new VzLinux 9.x and install a new Virtuozzo Server 9 Control Panel (with the name target-CP) either in interactive or unattended mode. Ensure your source-CP does not have unsupported features; otherwise, it will not allow you to perform the upgrade. Ensure both source-CP and target-CP are in the same management network and can reach each other. Ensure all hypervisors (compute resources) are online before starting the upgrade. The upgrade procedure log must be displayed via STDIN and appended to /onapp/interface/log/production_import_from_7_0.log. To upgrade Control Panel from CentOS 7 to Virtuozzo Server 9 Copy onapp user keys from source-CP to source-CP for the root user: ssh-copy-id -i /home/onapp/.ssh/id_rsa.pub root@SOURCE_IP_OR_HOSTNAMECopy ssh-copy-id -i /home/onapp/.ssh/id_rsa.pub root@SOURCE_IP_OR_HOSTNAME Copy onapp user keys from target-CP to source-CP for the root user: ssh-copy-id -i /home/onapp/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub root@SOURCE_IP_OR_HOSTNAMECopy ssh-copy-id -i /home/onapp/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub root@SOURCE_IP_OR_HOSTNAME Generate a new SSH key for the root user and copy it to source-CP: ssh-keygen -b 4096 -t rsa -q -f /root/.ssh/id_rsa -N "" &>/dev/null ssh-copy-id -i /root/.ssh/id_rsa.pub root@SOURCE_IP_OR_HOSTNAMECopy ssh-keygen -b 4096 -t rsa -q -f /root/.ssh/id_rsa -N "" &>/dev/null ssh-copy-id -i /root/.ssh/id_rsa.

chunks.title: Installing a Control Panel server with the Firstboot Installer
chunks.content: Installing a Control Panel server with the Firstboot Installer The Firstboot Installer is a user-friendly interface for installing a Control Panel server. With this system, you can easily set up the Control Panel server and use a log file to track all the logs performed during the installation. After installing Virtuozzo Server, you can proceed to set up a Control Panel server in interactive mode. To install a Control Panel server in interactive mode Use the arrow keys on the keyboard to move around the text in the system. In Virtuozzo Server 9.0 Installation, click the Reboot System button. Specify your login and select the Enter key on the keyboard. Enter your password and select the Enter key on the keyboard. In Installation type selection, select Cluster with Control Panel and use the Enter key on the keyboard to confirm your choice. In Cluster role selection, select Control Panel Server and use the Enter key on the keyboard to confirm your choice. In Control Panel Configuration, select one or more IP addresses for the SNMP daemon and use the Enter key on the keyboard to confirm your choice. Otherwise, manually specify one or more IP addresses (separated by a comma) for the SNMP daemon. After selecting or specifying the IP addresses for the SNMP daemon, select OK and use the Enter key on the keyboard to confirm your choice.

chunks.title: Installing a Control Panel server
chunks.content: Installing a Control Panel server Before you begin Install Control Panel on a server running the Virtuozzo Server 9 OS. Review Get Started to ensure your environment is ready for installation. Use the corresponding option of the Control Panel installer if MySQL is already installed and configured. The installer output is redirected to /onapp-cp-install.log. All the installer critical errors are written to /var/log/messages. To test the upgrade, you may first simulate the upgrade process on the test environment. For more details, refer to Configuring Control Panel Environment for Simulation Purposes. Disable SELinux before the installation. To install a Control Panel server Update your server: # yum updateCopy # yum update Install the packages required for the Virtuozzo OnApp YUM repository file: # yum install chkconfig initscriptsCopy # yum install chkconfig initscripts Install the Virtuozzo OnApp Control Panel installer package: # yum install onapp-cp-installCopy # yum install onapp-cp-install (Optional) You can set custom configuration options for Control Panel.
